text:
This looks like late 2012 to early 2013. The unemployment rate is 8.1%, the fed funds rate is about 0.14%, and the 10-year yield is 1.66%. Headline CPI is 1.7%.

US large-cap equity is up 26.7% over 12 months, which fits the period ending around September 2012 (the S&P 500 returned about 30% from September 2011 to September 2012). VIX at 14.84 also fits September 2012. The unemployment rate was 8.1% in August 2012 and 7.8% in September. Payroll growth averaged about 94k over three months, which matches August 2012. The 10-year yield was around 1.66% at the end of August 2012. Gold rose 7% in the month, consistent with August–September 2012.

Equity returns of +2.3% over 1 month, +6.3% over 3 months, and +26.7% over 12 months fit August 2012 reasonably. The S&P 500 was up about 2.3% in August 2012 after rising about 1.3% in July. Gold was up about 7% in the month of September 2012, but August was up around 5%, so the gold figure is a loose match. The 10-year yield ended August 2012 at about 1.57% and September at 1.63%, which favors September. But the 8.1% unemployment rate was the August reading, published in early September, so it fits a snapshot taken at the end of August. The 12-month equity return was about 18% in August 2012 and about 30% in September 2012, so +26.7% is closer to September, though the data is ambiguous. I'll go with August/September 2012, leaning August.
